raw_response:
I've farmed this land all my life, just like my father and grandfather before me. I don't know books, but I know this soil and I know what grows here. In Quzhou, we grow winter wheat and summer corn — that's what everyone does, that's what makes sense here on the flat land with the groundwater underneath us.

My wheat goes in around October, comes out in June. Then I plant corn right after, harvest in September. Same 10 mu of land does both. I don't need to think too hard about this — the rotation works, the market buys both, and I know how to do it.

I'll buy the improved wheat seeds from the township seed shop, the same kind I used last year. For corn, hybrid — everyone buys hybrid corn now, even I know hybrid corn yields more. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress urea when the plants need it. I irrigate the wheat four times: before winter sets in, at jointing, at heading, and when the grain is filling. Corn only needs water a couple times unless the summer is very dry.

I rotary-till before wheat planting to break up the stubble and level the field. For corn I just plant straight into the ground after wheat harvest — no time to till, need to get the seeds in quick.

I spray herbicide on the wheat in winter and spray again in spring if I see rust or aphids. For corn, one herbicide pass and watch for pests mid-season.
